questions.question: What will the U.S. CPI inflation rate be in calendar 2026?
questions.why_it_matters: Inflation is a shared economic quantity that can affect household purchasing power, business costs, and Federal Reserve policy, with potential consequences for financing conditions and market valuations. The article links inflation concerns to wage growth and possible rate increases, though it gives no U.S. CPI figure or explicit inflation forecast.
questions.why_not_already_covered: The existing questions do not track U.S. inflation. The article’s references to potential Federal Reserve rate hikes concern a possible policy response, not the inflation outcome itself; those outcomes can change independently.
questions.how_and_when_to_check: Check after the final relevant 2026 CPI release, using the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics’ CPI releases to assess the calendar-year inflation rate. The article supplies no CPI value or stated date for such a determination; December 31, 2026 is an analyst check date, not a date stated in the article.

article:
① A dense schedule of U.S. data releases in August, including employment figures, JOLTS, ADP, and ISM reports, will prompt the market to reassess the likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September; ② S&P 500 second-quarter earnings are projected to rise by 34.5% year-on-year, with performance from technology companies such as Broadcom serving as a test of whether corporate profits can continue to support U.S. equities.
Cailian Press, August 30 (Editor: Xia Junxiong) – This week, all three major U.S. stock indices recorded weekly gains. The S&P 500 rose by 0.49%, the Nasdaq Composite increased by 0.85%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed by 0.53%.
The S&P 500 is currently just over 1% below its historic high set on August 13. NVIDIA, the leader in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, released quarterly earnings on Wednesday that significantly exceeded expectations, boosting market sentiment. This followed earlier pressure on equities caused by rising U.S. Treasury yields earlier this month.
In the coming week, the market will refocus on the condition of the U.S. labor market, particularly the August non-farm payrolls data scheduled for release on Friday.
This report will provide two key insights for the market: first, the current resilience of the U.S. job market, and second, whether high inflation is further translating into wage growth. Investors are using this information to assess whether the Federal Reserve might raise interest rates as early as September.
Michael Reynolds, Vice President of Investment Strategy at Glenmede, stated: “As we approach the Federal Reserve’s September meeting, every data point will be scrutinized under a microscope, as each has the potential to influence the Fed’s final decision.”
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh emphasized in his recent speech at the Jackson Hole conference that inflation remains the core issue facing policymakers, hinting that further interest rate hikes may be necessary in the coming months.
Data indicates that the U.S. money market currently assigns a 57% probability to a 25-basis-point rate hike by the Federal Reserve in September, with expectations of at least one rate hike before December fully priced in.
James Knightley, an economist at ING, stated in a report: “We expect a modest rebound of approximately 65,000 jobs in August, but the pattern of ‘low hiring and low layoffs’ is likely to persist. Caution related to tariffs and higher financing costs may extend this situation through the remainder of the year.”
Prior to the release of the non-farm payrolls data on Friday, the market will receive additional indicators regarding the U.S. labor market.
The U.S. JOLTS job openings data for July will be released on Tuesday; the ADP private sector employment report for August will be published on Wednesday; and the weekly initial jobless claims will be announced on Thursday.
Other key data reflecting current economic activity include the ISM Manufacturing Index for August, to be released on Tuesday, and the ISM Services Index for August, to be released on Thursday. U.S. factory orders data for July will also be published on Wednesday.
As the second-quarter earnings season for U.S. stocks draws to a close, Broadcom’s results, scheduled for release on Wednesday, will also be in the spotlight. Additionally, companies such as Dell Technologies and Hewlett Packard Enterprise will report their earnings.
Broadcom currently has a market capitalization of approximately $1.7 trillion. Previously, strong earnings from its competitor NVIDIA had already driven major stock indices higher.
NVIDIA expects its revenue for the next fiscal year to surge by 70%. This represents a relatively rare disclosure for the AI bellwether, as NVIDIA typically does not provide performance forecasts over such an extended horizon.
Matt Stucky, Chief Equity Portfolio Manager at Northwestern Mutual Wealth Management, stated, “What we want to know now is whether Broadcom will also offer a similar level of earnings visibility.”
With the vast majority of companies having completed their earnings disclosures, adjusted second-quarter earnings for S&P 500 constituents are projected to rise by 34.5% year-on-year, according to LSEG IBES data.
Michael Reynolds, Vice President of Investment Strategy at Glenmede, noted that this earnings season has demonstrated “very robust core profitability.”
He added, “If the results reported by the final batch of companies in the coming week can sustain this performance, I believe it would send a very positive signal for the market outlook for the remainder of the year.”
Overview of key international economic events next week (Beijing time):
Monday (August 31): U.S. Dallas Fed Business Activity Index for August; Germany CPI for August
Tuesday (September 1): Eurozone August CPI; final Manufacturing PMI for France, Germany, and the Eurozone in August; final UK August Manufacturing PMI; final S&P Global US August Manufacturing PMI; US August ISM Manufacturing PMI; US July JOLTS Job Openings
Wednesday (September 2): US July factory orders month-on-month change; Bank of Canada interest rate decision; Reserve Bank of New Zealand interest rate decision and Monetary Policy Statement; Australia Q2 GDP; US August ADP Employment Change
Thursday (September 3): Federal Reserve Beige Book; Eurozone July PPI; US July trade balance; US August ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI; final S&P Global US August Services/Composite PMI; final Services/Composite PMI for France, Germany, and the Eurozone in August
Friday (September 4): US August seasonally adjusted non-farm payrolls; US August unemployment rate; Eurozone July retail sales
